title: Horizons Summit 2026
headline: JFF's two-day national summit on workforce development, education, and economic opportunity, bringing together 2,000+ leaders in Washington, DC.
shortSummary: Horizons Summit 2026, organized by Jobs for the Future (JFF), is a two-day in-person conference in Washington, DC, focused on workforce development, education, and economic opportunity. It convenes employers, investors, government leaders, entrepreneurs, and education providers in a nonpartisan environment, with 60+ sessions, six networking breaks, and 2,000+ attendees.
mediumSummary: Horizons Summit 2026 is Jobs for the Future's (JFF) annual national platform for driving equitable economic advancement. Held July 13-14, 2026, at the Marriott Marquis in Washington, DC, the two-day summit convenes employers, investors, government leaders, entrepreneurs, and education and training providers across sectors. The program features 60+ sessions and six networking breaks, drawing more than 2,000 leaders and changemakers. detailedOverview:
Horizons Summit 2026 is a two-day in-person conference organized by Jobs for the Future (JFF), a national nonprofit headquartered in Boston that drives transformation of the U.S. education and workforce systems. The summit, held July 13-14, 2026, at the Marriott Marquis Washington, DC, is JFF's trusted national platform for equitable economic advancement, founded in 2016.

The event convenes a cross-sector audience of employers, investors, government leaders, entrepreneurs, and education and training providers in a nonpartisan environment. According to the event program, it includes 60+ sessions, six networking breaks, and more than 2,000 attendees described as leaders and changemakers. Stated focus areas include actionable strategies, partnership opportunities, and influencing the future of workforce and education policy.

Conference themes center on expanding access to quality jobs, economic mobility, workforce development, education, and job creation. The main-stage program features conversations with leaders from industry and policy, including remarks on what makes a quality job.

In conjunction with the main summit, JFF runs its inaugural Legislative Summit on July 13-14 at the Marriott Marquis and on July 15 on Capitol Hill. Participation in the Legislative Summit is limited and invite-based: attendees must be paid Horizons registrants, complete a questionnaire, be accepted, and pay an additional $100 fee. The Legislative Summit includes breakfast with congressional staff and constituent meetings with congressional offices.

Registration is handled through the Horizons registration portal at horizons.jff.org, with tiered pricing and rate increases announced through mid-May 2026.
